quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: In a motor vehicle on a highway, is it legal to drink or have open alcohol containers?

options.text: No. It is illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers.
Yes, if you are not driving.
Yes, if you are driving but not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. It is illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of alcohol. Drivers and passengers cannot have open alcohol containers in a moving vehicle.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to let you go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: A car is following you too closely on a two-lane road. What should you do?

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed so the other driver will pass you.
Speed up to create more distance.
Tap your brakes to slow down, then speed up again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed so the other driver will pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, change lanes if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This encourages the other driver to pass you.

questions.question: An oncoming car's headlights are too bright. Where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road.
At the right side of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by the bright headlights. This lets you see the road and stay in your lane. Do not keep your bright lights on in response.

questions.question: You are parking uphill on a road with a curb. Which way should your front wheels point?

options.text: Toward the curb.
Away from the curb.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail and your car rolls backward, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When you merge onto a freeway, what speed should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto a freeway at or near the speed of traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up a little.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep your speed the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill. A vehicle may be stopped ahead. Slow down as you approach hills or curves so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you may cross it to pass another vehicle when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped yellow sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning of danger ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning of danger ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped yellow signs warn of possible danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn of dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children, regardless of which direction you are driving.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When you are following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a collision. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from behind, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. Press your body against the back of your seat and your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Be ready to apply brakes to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Know you are traveling in the wrong direction.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Wait until it turns green before you can proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will give you space to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will give you space to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space or let you pass. Always make sure the space is clear before you move into it.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Release the gas pedal slowly.
Slow down by pumping the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal slowly.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas pedal and avoid using the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before steering or stopping.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it by following the law.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. Smooth steering and braking help you control your vehicle safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction the arrow points. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines separate:

options.text: No-passing zones.
Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed yellow lines mean passing is allowed when it is safe.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space to safely move back in front of the other vehicle.

questions.question: How do you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Change to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for cars entering the freeway. If you can, move to the next lane to create a gap. If you cannot move, adjust your speed to let them enter safely and smoothly.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many cars pass you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane so you don't slow down traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let cars pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic around you, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: What speed should you always travel at?

options.text: The speed of the cars around you.
The speed limit.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed depends on the road, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Your car has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS). What should you do if you need to stop quickly?

options.text: Press the brake pedal hard and hold it down.
Pump the brake pedal.
Press the brake pedal slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal hard and hold it down.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep it pressed. The ABS will pump the brakes very fast. Do not release the pedal because ABS only works when you press down fully.

questions.question: You want to enter the freeway but do not see a gap in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make a gap.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: If you do not see a gap, slow down on the ramp and wait. Do not drive to the end of the ramp and stop. You need room to speed up to match traffic before you enter the freeway.
